name: Challow
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog cites only Ivani 2024 (languoid establishment, no title/details shown); no description of Challow stress located

tone_statements.citation: Ivani, Jessica K. 2023. Challow language from northeastern India: a field report. In: HLS 26 abstracts, 4-6 September 2023, Paris (26th Himalayan Languages Symposium, INALCO), p. 36. [Abstract in the booklet of abstracts; the talk does not appear in the final, so it may not have been delivered.]
tone_statements.quote: Challow linguistic profile aligns in principle with the traits identified in the Tibeto-Burman languages spoken in the area by including, among other features, sesquisyllabic syllables (Matisoff 2003) and various `frozen’ formatives prefixed to the stem of several nouns, verbs and adjectives, common in the Ukhrul district (Mortensen 2003, Ivani 2023) and beyond (Matisoff 2003). In addition, Challow exhibits lexical tone and SOV word order; noun morphology is mostly agglutinative and displays monoexponential case markers and ergative-absolutive alignment.
tone_statements.summary: Challow is stated to have lexical tone; no inventory, no count of tones, no examples of tonal minimal pairs; tone-bearing unit not stated here (the HL 22(2) paper places [T] at the syllable level, bracketed as uncertain).

sources.citation: Ivani, Jessica K. 2024 [eScholarship cover page dates it 2023; CrossRef issued 2023-08-20]. Some preliminary notes on Challow, a Trans-Himalayan language from Manipur, India. Himalayan Linguistics 22(2) (Languages and Peoples of the Eastern Himalayan Region): 1-12. DOI 10.5070/H922259698. CC BY-NC-ND.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the 13-page PDF (a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence/pitch/prosody: zero hits). Section 2 'Phonological properties' gives the syllable template (C2)C1V(Cf)[T] (Figure 1, p.3), sesquisyllabic frozen prefixes with reduced centralized vowels (p.3, 2.4 pp.7-8), initials (2.2) and rhymes (2.3). Only prosodic remark, p.3: 'This study will not deal with tone; however, an impressionistic account of the data supported by comparative materials suggests that Challow has contrastive lexical tone (T) at the syllable level.' sources.note: No stress content. Confirms Ivani 2024 is the sole reference: 'Challow.. is first mentioned in Jessica K. Ivani 2024. It is not intelligible to neighbouring languages and thus constitutes a separate (probably Tangkhulic) language.' AES status threatened.

sources.citation: Ivani, Jessica K. 2023. Challow language from northeastern India: a field report. In: HLS 26 abstracts, 4-6 September 2023, Paris (26th Himalayan Languages Symposium, INALCO), p. 36. [Abstract in the booklet of abstracts; the talk does not appear in the final, so it may not have been delivered.]
sources.quote: Challow linguistic profile aligns in principle with the traits identified in the Tibeto-Burman languages spoken in the area by including, among other features, sesquisyllabic syllables (Matisoff 2003) and various `frozen’ formatives prefixed to the stem of several nouns, verbs and adjectives, common in the Ukhrul district (Mortensen 2003, Ivani 2023) and beyond (Matisoff 2003). In addition, Challow exhibits lexical tone and SOV word order; noun morphology is mostly agglutinative and displays monoexponential case markers and ergative-absolutive alignment.
sources.note: One-page conference abstract; para. 2 states flatly that 'Challow exhibits lexical tone' (alongside sesquisyllabic syllables, frozen prefixes, SOV order, agglutinative noun morphology, ergative-absolutive alignment). No number of tones, no tonal contrasts exemplified, no domain stated; the abstract promises discussion of 'phonotactics, phonology, syllable structure' in the talk. Firmer wording than the hedge in the published HL 22(2) paper ('impressionistic account.. suggests that Challow has contrastive lexical tone (T) at the syllable level'), but still an assertion without an inventory.
